changes: Scribe's stem name normalized to IAST 'Govindadāsa'. The colophon has the anusvāra spelling 'goviṃdadāsa', which stays in as_written.

Viṣṇupurī given the role 'commentator' as well as 'author' (medium confidence). The colophon says the work is 'sakāṃtimālā' (with the Kāntimālā), and the Kāntimālā is usually ascribed to Viṣṇupurī himself.
Place as_written extended to include 'kalyāṇaśayake'. The likely identification is added to notes, but normalized is left empty.
Notes expanded on the tairabhukta epithet and on the place.

notes: 'vivekatairabhaktasya' is probably a corruption of '...viveka-tairabhukta-', i.e. a native of Tirabhukti (Tirhut, Mithilā). That fits the tradition that Viṣṇupurī came from Mithilā. Puruṣottama in the opening epithet is the deity (Jagannātha) and is not a person. The text is the Bhaktiratnāvalī with its commentary Kāntimālā, which is usually ascribed to Viṣṇupurī himself. Āmāvatī is probably Āmbāvatī/Amber (Āmer, near Jaipur), but this is not certain. 'kalyāṇaśayake' may be a corruption of 'kalyāṇarāyake' (a Kalyāṇarāya temple?), which would fit the closing 'śrīkalyāṇayannamaḥ'. VS 1673 Āśvina śukla 12 falls in about September/October 1616 CE. Nothing marks this as a Nepalese copy.
